errors.english: (Devadatta) a standard placeholder name in Indian philosophy, like John Doe
errors.why: The Tibetan says only 'like Devadatta walking'; the explanatory phrase is unmarked editorial content inserted into the running translation.

note: A careful lemma-by-lemma rendering of the commentary; only an unmarked inline gloss intrudes.

errors.english: Even in those who are innocent, suspicion arises because of the sins I have committed.
errors.why: The queen says that, having sinned, she herself grows suspicious even of insentient things (sems med, Skt. niścetaneṣv api), not that suspicion arises in innocent people.

fix.find: Even in those who are innocent, suspicion arises because of the sins I have committed.
fix.replace: Because of the sin I have committed, suspicion arises in me even toward things without minds.

errors.english: [note: Mayuriraja, referring to a specific character or a queen with peacock-like qualities]
errors.why: The 'peacock queen' is a peacock in the palace that speaks human speech (Skt. mayūrarājaḥ … puruṣālāpaveṣṭitaḥ), not a woman with peacock-like qualities; the note misleads about who is poisoned.

errors.english: [note: referring to the secret of her infidelity or crime]
errors.why: The thorn lodged in the palace is the peacock itself (śalyamayaṃ sthitam antaḥpure), the witness who may tell the king, not the secret.

note: The narrative line is followed, but the queen's self-suspicion is turned into suspicion of the innocent and the notes misidentify the peacock.

errors.why: The Nyāya jāti rendered khyad par med pa mtshungs pa is aviśeṣasama, not 'abhedasama'.

note: The argument about vikalpasama and aviśeṣasama is followed accurately; only the Sanskrit equivalent in a note is off.
A faithful rendering of the Vinaya commentary on theft by displacement, including the root-text citation and variant reading.

errors.english: only the nature of the effect itself serves as the substantial cause of the occasional and continuous causes, such as fire, clay, and the like,
errors.why: The Tibetan makes the causes of the state and of the continuum (fire, clay, etc.) the substantial causes of the effect's own nature only; the English reverses cause and effect.

fix.find: only the nature of the effect itself serves as the substantial cause of the occasional and continuous causes, such as fire, clay, and the like,
fix.replace: the causes of the state and of the continuum, such as fire, clay, and the like, are substantial causes only of the very nature of the effect,

errors.english: the distinction established by the presence and absence of fire possessing molten copper
errors.why: The point is that fire, a distinct thing apprehended through positive and negative concomitance with the molten state of copper, is shown to be an auxiliary condition; fire does not 'possess molten copper'.

note: The broad mind-body argument is recognisable, but the closing sentences on substantial versus auxiliary causes are garbled, one with cause and effect reversed.

errors.english: two types based on consequence and essential nature through commitment
errors.why: The two further types are kinds of commitment-based inference relying on an imputed effect-reason and an imputed nature-reason (scripture and common renown); 'bras bu is effect, not 'consequence', and brtags pa is dropped.

fix.find: two types based on consequence and essential nature through commitment
fix.replace: two types of commitment-based inference, relying on an imputed effect and an imputed nature

errors.english: In this context, "perception and so forth" refers to the means of knowledge.
errors.why: The lemma is 'de la' ('among these') and the gloss is 'perception and so forth'; the English inverts lemma and gloss.

fix.find: In this context, "perception and so forth" refers to the means of knowledge.
fix.replace: "Among these" means among perception and so forth.

errors.english: If the excluded is not a thesis according to the (pramāṇas) valid means of knowledge
errors.why: The question is: if what is refuted by the pramāṇas is not a thesis, how is it explained as fourfold; the pramāṇas are the agents of refutation, not the authority for the claim.

errors.english: refers to the treatises one accepts as a subject
errors.why: The gloss says the word for the subjective act of acceptance (yul can) metonymically indicates the accepted treatise; 'as a subject' misreads yul can.

note: The pakṣa discussion is broadly followed, but the fourfold division of invalidation and the lemma-gloss structure at the end are mishandled.

errors.english: Not of a single color, nor white with a fringe.
errors.why: The verse lists three separately prohibited kinds of garment (single-coloured, fringed, white), as the commentary then explains; 'white with a fringe' merges two items.

note: A sound rendering of the śrāmaṇera dress rules; one verse list is mis-segmented.

errors.english: The Root of the Wish-Fulfilling Vine
errors.why: The colophon says the Farmer's avadāna is the sixty-first branch 'from' the Wish-Fulfilling Vine; there is no 'Root'.
lug is 'sheep' (Skt. ūrṇāyu, the wool-bearer), so the settlement is full of sheep, not wool.

note: The opening of the Farmer's avadāna is rendered faithfully apart from small slips in the colophon and opening verse.
The objection about distinct and non-distinct continua and the commentator's reply are rendered accurately, with speakers correctly assigned.

errors.why: ltag chod is the technical term jāti (futile rejoinder), not tarka.

errors.english: of the nature of perceiving a pervading contradiction
errors.why: The term is viruddhavyāptopalabdhi, 'observation of what is pervaded by a contradictory', a specific type of negative reason.

errors.english: For whichever entity has a different nature—specifically the sprout—
errors.why: The entity is the one determined toward another nature, the sprout (i.e. the cause), not the sprout itself.

errors.english: this shows that there is no dependence on general arising or destruction
errors.why: 'In general' qualifies the showing: the principle shows generally that, for arising or destruction, there is no dependence; it is not 'general arising'.

note: The commentary's lemmas are tracked, but key logical terms (jāti, viruddhavyāptopalabdhi) are mistranslated and some referents confused.
